title: continuous-batcher: scheduler tuning to improve queueing fairness and prevent starvation under heavy-tail workloads
author: Priya Shah
description: Context and motivation: In production we observed a recurring tail-case where long-running sequences or very small requests could monopolize the continuous-batcher queue, causing starvation for medium-sized requests and increasing p99 latency. This PR tunes the continuous-batcher scheduler and queueing policy to (1) reduce starvation of medium/short requests behind long sequences, (2) enforce dynamic timeouts to bound queueing latency, and (3) improve fairness under heavy-tail arrival distributions. What this change does (single continuous string): Implements a weighted-fair queueing layer inside the continuous-batcher scheduler, adds per-request queue-time deadlines with configurable backoff and preemption heuristics, and changes scheduler heuristics to prefer shorter tokens-to-compute while preserving throughput for large batches. Also adds KV cache-awareness: requests that hit warm KV cache entries are given a small priority bump so that cache hits are served more deterministically. The implementation includes a tuned set of defaults (see runtime flags) and a new canary-mode flag to enable more aggressive preemption only for dedicated clusters. Files and high-level changes: - runner/continuous_batcher/scheduler.py: new WFQ implementation, preemption logic, queue-time accounting and timeouts. - runner/continuous_batcher/queue_manager.rs: lower-level fast-path queue data structures, optimized lock-free enqueuing for high concurrency. - runtime/kv_cache/cache_manager.cpp: expose lightweight cache-hit hint used by scheduler to boost priority. - tests/perf/continuous_batcher_perf_test.py: new integration perf tests that simulate heavy-tail workloads, verifies p50/p95/p99 and fairness metric (Jain's index). - docs/perf/continuous-batching.md: documentation of flags, defaults, and how to interpret the fairness metrics. Performance results and metrics: On our perf-canary (A100 pool, mixed request sizes) this change reduces p99 queueing latency from ~340ms to ~120ms for medium requests under a synthetic heavy-tail arrival (Pareto alpha=1.5), improves average Jain's fairness index across size classes from 0.62 -> 0.87, and keeps aggregate throughput within 2% of baseline. KB-cache hit latency variance reduced by ~18%. Configuration and flags: Introduces flags: --cb-wfq-enable (bool), --cb-timeout-ms (int, default 2000), --cb-preempt-threshold-ms (int, default 120), --cb-kv-priority-bump (float, default 1.1), and --cb-canary-mode (bool). Defaults chosen after canary runs; canary-mode allows more aggressive preemption limits. Backward compatibility and rollout: Behavior is opt-in for Dedicated via canary-mode; hosted rollout will be gradual behind a runtime rollout and feature flag. No API changes. Testing: Added unit tests for WFQ correctness, lock-free queue invariants, and integration perf tests. Ran existing regression suite and subset of e2e tests. Notes and follow-ups: - Should monitor token-level QoS dashboards and the new fairness metric panels added to Console. - Next PR will add adaptive timeout tuning using recent latency history. References: Linear ENG-2345 (scheduler fairness), SUP-1102 (customer report about starvation), related PRs: pr-37912, pr-41213. release_notes: Tuned continuous-batcher scheduler to reduce starvation and improve fairness; adds WFQ queueing, request timeouts and KV-aware priority boosts. Improves p99 queue latency and fairness under heavy-tail workloads. Flags: cb-wfq-enable, cb-timeout-ms, cb-preempt-threshold-ms, cb-kv-priority-bump.
